choices.text: Reserve the official block at $231/night, refundable, in-room coffee and fridge listed, no room-rate morning meal shown; verify the basics and use the in-hotel briefing.
Reserve Residence Inn Pearl at $199/night, refundable, kitchenette and morning meal in the rate, but a 10-to-12-minute walk or rideshare to the ballroom.
Reserve Hyatt Place downtown at $213/night, refundable, room basics and morning meal in the rate, but a longer walk and less direct session access.
Reserve the Courtyard next door at $214/night, refundable, bistro items sold separately, fridge by request, and a slightly lower nightly rate than the block.

candidate.difficulty_rationale: Residence Inn is cheaper and includes the hotel service she often values, so it is a strong near miss. The history is needed to recognize that meeting-provided breakfast plus concentrated in-building sessions can outweigh the ordinary preference.
candidate.gold_action: Reserve the official block and verify the room basics, treating the agenda-provided breakfast and in-building sessions as the controlling context.
candidate.label_rationale: The included-breakfast tendency is not absolute. In the Minneapolis board meeting, its value dropped when breakfast was part of the meeting; in Minneapolis, Philadelphia, and Phoenix conference-style trips she accepted the meeting hotel when it reduced agenda risk and was reimbursable. Those were contextual exceptions, not permanent revisions away from the included-service default. This Portland scenario has the same boundary: a mandatory in-hotel breakfast briefing and most sessions in the block hotel make the official block the lower-friction hold.
candidate.query: Marisol is narrowing lodging for a Portland policy convening. The Wednesday agenda begins with a mandatory 7:45 a.m. breakfast briefing in the official hotel ballroom, and most sessions stay in that building. Her office will reimburse the block if she notes the meeting location. Which action is most consistent with her history?

leakage_signals: Objective cue sufficient to answer: mandatory breakfast briefing and sessions in the official hotel, with the block reimbursable.
query_only_verdict.rationale: The mandatory 7:45 a.m. breakfast briefing and most sessions are in the official hotel, and the office will reimburse the block. A keeps her in the event building and lists the room basics; the lack of a room-rate breakfast is not material because the agenda breakfast is in-house.

choices.text: Buy the Riverside package now and preserve the $42 saving; treat breakfast available daily and the lobby coffee as sufficient for this short stay.
Book Hyatt Place now and stop evaluating the package, because the package wording and request-only refrigerator are not worth any further checking.
Place a refundable Hyatt Place hold and ask Riverside to confirm whether the package rate includes the same morning and room basics; switch only if the net value remains real.
Buy the Riverside package but add a grocery stop or rideshare budget so any paid morning food and refrigerator uncertainty are absorbed.

candidate.difficulty_rationale: Both B and C avoid assuming the package is adequate, and A is tempting on price. The long-history distinction is that Marisol usually asks or checks unclear inclusions before giving up a potentially useful option, rather than treating ambiguity itself as a hard disqualifier.
candidate.gold_action: Hold Hyatt Place as the confirmed fallback, then verify whether Riverside's package rate actually includes the morning service and room basics before deciding.
candidate.label_rationale: She has repeatedly treated ambiguous wording such as breakfast being available, hotel buffet language, or an unconfirmed block inclusion as something to check rather than assume. The preference is still soft: she should not permanently reject a cheaper package solely because the page is vague if it can be verified. The best action is therefore to protect the confirmed included-rate option while asking Riverside the specific inclusion questions.
candidate.query: Boise community-arts site visit: the flights are settled, but the lodging can be bought as a package or separately. The package with Riverside Lodge is $42 less total; its page says breakfast available daily, coffee in the lobby, refrigerator by request, and the package becomes fee-cancelable after 24 hours. The same flights plus Hyatt Place downtown cost $42 more; that hotel is refundable until two days out and lists a king room, mini-fridge, coffee maker, and morning buffet in the standard rate. Both locations work for dinner and an 8:30 host pickup. What should the assistant recommend before payment?

leakage_signals: No private-history cue is needed; ambiguous package inclusions and stricter cancellation create an objective reason to hold the clear refundable option and verify before payment.
query_only_verdict.rationale: C preserves optionality before payment: Hyatt is refundable and has clear room and morning basics, while Riverside's savings may disappear if breakfast/fridge are not actually included and its package cancellation becomes restrictive after 24 hours.

choices.text: Hotel Providence block at $207: at the pickup point and dinner block, in-room coffee and fridge listed, with breakfast not included in the standard rate.
Hampton downtown at $182: room basics and morning meal in the rate, but outside the pickup zone and a 12-minute morning rideshare away.
Aloft riverfront at $171: cheapest and decent dinner walk, paid grab-and-go items, with mini-fridge by request.
Residence Inn university area at $225: kitchen and morning meal in the rate, but a 15-minute ride from the pickup point.

candidate.difficulty_rationale: A generic planner could prefer the cheaper Hampton because the rideshare is short and it includes the morning service. The long-history policy is needed to avoid over-applying the included-breakfast preference when a current-trip logistics constraint is stronger.
candidate.gold_action: Hold the Hotel Providence block and verify any room-rate details, rather than moving outside the host pickup zone solely for the morning meal.
candidate.label_rationale: Her history supports breakfast as a recurring factor, but also shows it is not a hard veto. She has chosen lower-friction event or meeting hotels when the agenda, pickup, or meeting location made them more defensible. The Hampton is a strong near miss because it follows the included-service pattern and is cheaper, but this scenario adds a concrete host-pickup constraint and materials handling, so the no-car logistics should win. That boundary is a one-trip application, not a permanent weakening of the preference.
candidate.query: Providence site visit lodging is down to four refundable options. The host can do a 7:35 a.m. lobby pickup only at the state arts-council hotel; otherwise Marisol must rideshare to the pickup point with site materials. Dinner is easiest downtown. Which recommendation best matches her prior tradeoffs?

leakage_signals: Objective cue sufficient to answer: host pickup is available only at the state arts-council hotel; otherwise she must rideshare with materials.
query_only_verdict.rationale: A is at the only lobby pickup point and in the easiest dinner block, avoiding an early rideshare with site materials. It also lists in-room coffee and fridge, so its lack of included breakfast is outweighed by the stated pickup logistics.

choices.text: Holiday Inn Express at $171: ten-minute drive, standard room, fridge/coffee listed, and a simple morning offering in the rate.
Embassy Suites at $185: ten-minute drive, larger suite, fridge/coffee listed, and a made-to-order morning meal in the rate.
21c Museum Hotel at $166: walkable design hotel, easy cafés nearby, room fridge by request, and breakfast purchased separately.
Residence Inn at $188: kitchenette and morning offering in the rate, but about a twenty-minute drive to the tour.

candidate.difficulty_rationale: For only $14 more, Embassy Suites offers a larger room and a better breakfast, so a planner might think it is the safest personalization choice. The history requires the finer boundary: included and simple is useful, but Marisol has not made a full-service breakfast a standing requirement.
candidate.gold_action: Book the Holiday Inn Express rather than upgrading mainly for a fuller morning meal or choosing the boutique option with a separate breakfast stop.
candidate.label_rationale: Her history supports a preference for included breakfast on personal or early-morning stays, but it does not show a requirement for a large or premium breakfast. The Holiday Inn Express gives the relevant included service and room basics at a simple price. Embassy Suites is a near miss because it over-satisfies one part of the pattern, while 21c is attractive generically but would create the separate morning purchase she often tries to avoid.
candidate.query: Lexington overnight before an 8:20 a.m. campus tour with Lena. They arrive after dinner, leave town right after the tour, and just need a clean refundable room with free parking. Which booking best fits Marisol's pattern without overbuilding the stay?

leakage_signals: Objective cue sufficient to answer: "just need" a clean room and "without overbuilding" point to the simple standard option.
query_only_verdict.rationale: The query specifies a simple clean overnight with free parking, after-dinner arrival, departure right after the tour, and not overbuilding the stay. A is the standard short-drive option with fridge/coffee and a simple included morning offering; B and D are larger/kitchenette options, and C adds design-hotel/paid-breakfast/fridge-by-request tradeoffs for only a small saving.
